1 هَبَتَهُ , aor.
هَبِتَ , (inf. n. هَبْتٌ, TA,) He beat, struck, or smote, him (A, 'Obeyd, S, K) with a sword. (Sh.) Ex. هَبتُوهُمَا حَتَّى فَرَغُوا مِنْهُمَا They smote them both with swords until they slew them (TA, from trad.) ―
-b2- هَبَتَهُ, aor.
هَبِتَ , He, or it, lowered him, syn. هَبَطَهُ and طَأْطَأَهُ and حطَّهُ. (K,) with respect to station, rank, or dignity (TA:) and abased him; debased him; rendered him abject, vile, despicable, or ignominious. (L.) Ex. هَبَتَهُ المَوْتُ عِنْدِى منْزلَةً Death lowered him in my estimation with respect to rank, or dignity, because he died upon his bed. and did not die a martyr. From a trad. (Fr.) ―
-b3- هُبِتَ He was lowered with respect to rank, station, or dignity. (Fr.) ―
-b4- هُبِتَ (like عُنِىَ, [i. e. pass. in form, but neut. in signification,] (K,) He (a man) was cowardly, and his intellect quitted him: (S, K:) he was without intellect. (TA.) ―
-b5- هَبَتَ, aor. ?? see هَبِيتٌ.
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
